raw_case_text:
A 46-year-old male with no significant medical history presented with shortness of breath and flu-like symptoms including generalized weakness, fatigue, chills, diaphoresis, fever, and cough. The patient denied any recent sick contacts, travel history, history of shortness of breath, or history of lung disease. The patient reported only smoking conventional marijuana for 20 plus years, smoking 2 to 3 times per day, and had approximately a 4-6-month history of vape pen usage, with and without flavor additives. The cannabis vape pens were purchased in bulk from an informal source. The patient reported a less than 1-year history of conventional cigarette use and quit over 20 years ago. He denied the use of chewing tobacco, electronic cigarettes containing nicotine, or any other nicotine-containing products during this time.
On arrival, the patient was afebrile with a respiratory rate of 20 breaths per minute, oxygen saturation was 96% on ambient air, blood pressure was 126/82 mmHg, and heart rate was 96 beats per minute. Over the next 4 hours, the patient rapidly deteriorated into acute hypoxic respiratory failure with hypoxia down to 86% while on 2 liters nasal cannula. The patient was increased to 13 liters high-flow nasal cannula, started on empiric antibiotics, and intravenous methylprednisolone 125 mg which corrected the hypoxia with sustained oxygen saturation of 94%.
Physical exam was remarkable for diaphoresis, tachypnea, labored breathing with accessory muscle use, and diffuse inspiratory crackles. An arterial blood gas showed a pH of 7.51 [7.35-7.45], pCO2 38 [35-45 mmHg], pO2 84 [80-100 mmHg], and HCO3 of 30.3 mmol/L [22-26 mmol/L]. Lab work showed a venous lactic acidosis at 2.3 mmol/L [0.9-1.7 mmol/L], white blood cell count of 14.8 x 103/mul [4.4 - 10.5 x 103/mul], and a normal sedimentation rate. Chest X-ray noted diffuse, bilateral pulmonary consolidation sparing the apices, and bases with bronchopulmonary cuffing (Figure 1). Computed tomography (CT) imaging showed extensive bilateral airspace disease with increased reticulation, traction bronchiectasis, and ground glass opacities but noted sparing of apical spaces bilaterally (Figure 2).
Further lab work including blood and sputum cultures, HIV, urine Histoplasma, Legionella, Pneumococcal antigens, and respiratory viral panel were all negative. Serologies:coccidiomycosis, histoplasmosis, and pneumocystis:were also negative. Bronchoscopy with transbronchial biopsies were performed and a sample from the right lower lobe was significant for intra-alveolar inflammation including foamy macrophages and activated type II pneumocytes (Figure 3). These findings were consistent with organizing pneumonia. A histopathology examination on bronchoalveolar lavage (BAL) sample stained with Oil red O showed numerous lipid-laden macrophages and intra-alveolar macrophages containing blackish-brown pigment (Figure 4). This was consistent with a diagnosis of lipoid pneumonia. Additional testing was negative for AFB stain, cytomegalovirus, herpes simplex antigen, and aspergillus antigen. During the hospital course, the patient improved over a six-day regimen of bronchodilators, steroids, and empiric antibiotics with supportive care of oxygen supplementation. He was discharged on the same regimen for 14 days with follow-up with pulmonology and repeat CT imaging in six weeks.

subjective.chief_complaint: A 46-year-old male presented with shortness of breath and flu-like symptoms including fever, chills, diaphoresis, cough, and generalized weakness after 4 to 6 months of using informal-source cannabis vape pens.
subjective.history_of_present_illness: With no baseline pulmonary disease, the patient presented with acute dyspnea, cough, fever, chills, diaphoresis, and fatigue following 4-6 months of vaping cannabis cartridges (with and without flavor additives) purchased in bulk from an informal source. Within 4 hours of emergency department arrival, his oxygen saturation dropped from 96% on ambient air to 86% on 2 L/min nasal cannula, requiring escalation to 13 L/min high-flow nasal cannula.
subjective.past_medical_history: No significant medical history; 20+ year history of smoking conventional marijuana (2-3 times/day) and a 4-6 month history of using informal-market cannabis vape pens; quit conventional cigarettes >20 years ago (<1 year use) and denied nicotine e-cigarette use, recent travel, or sick contacts.
subjective.review_of_systems: Positive for shortness of breath, cough, fever, chills, diaphoresis, fatigue, and generalized weakness.

objective.physical_examination: Initial vitals: afebrile, respiratory rate 20 breaths/min, SpO2 96% on room air (dropping within 4 hours to 86% on 2 L/min NC), BP 126/82 mmHg, and heart rate 96 bpm. Physical exam during respiratory deterioration showed diaphoresis, tachypnea, labored breathing with accessory muscle use, and diffuse inspiratory crackles.
objective.routine_investigations: ABG showed pH 7.51, PaCO2 38 mmHg, PaO2 84 mmHg, and HCO3 30.3 mmol/L. Labs showed venous lactate 2.3 mmol/L (normal 0.9-1.7), leukocytosis (WBC 14.8 x 10^3/uL), and normal ESR. Blood and sputum cultures, HIV test, urinary Histoplasma, Legionella, and pneumococcal antigens, respiratory viral panel, and serologies for Coccidioides, Histoplasma, and Pneumocystis were all negative. Chest X-ray showed diffuse bilateral mid-zone pulmonary consolidation sparing the apices and bases with peribronchial cuffing.
objective.advanced_workup: Chest CT demonstrated extensive bilateral ground-glass opacities, increased reticular markings, and traction bronchiectasis with bilateral apical sparing. Bronchoscopy with bronchoalveolar lavage (BAL) tested negative for Aspergillus antigen, AFB stain, CMV, and HSV antigen; Oil Red O staining of BAL cytospin revealed numerous lipid-laden alveolar macrophages and macrophages containing blackish-brown pigment, and right lower lobe transbronchial lung biopsy demonstrated intra-alveolar foamy macrophages and reactive type II pneumocytes consistent with organizing and exogenous lipoid pneumonia.

assessment_and_plan.assessment_and_confirmation: E-cigarette, or vaping, product use-associated lung injury (EVALI) presenting as acute exogenous lipoid pneumonia and organizing pneumonia from informal-source cannabis vape pen use, confirmed by bilateral apical-sparing ground-glass opacities on chest CT, lipid-laden macrophages on BAL Oil Red O staining, and foamy macrophage/organizing alveolitis on transbronchial biopsy after ruling out pulmonary aspergillosis and other fungal, bacterial, and viral infections. Treated with high-flow nasal cannula oxygen, intravenous methylprednisolone (125 mg) followed by a 14-day oral corticosteroid taper, bronchodilators, and empirical antibiotics, achieving rapid correction of hypoxemia and hospital discharge on day 6.
